module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 757

*References:*
 - [erdosproblems.com/757](https://www.erdosproblems.com/757)
 - [GyLe95] Gyárfás, András and Lehel, Jenő, Linear sets with five distinct differences among any
    four elements. J. Combin. Theory Ser. B (1995), 108-118.
-/

@[expose] public section

open scoped Pointwise
open Filter

namespace Erdos757

/-- We say that `c` is admissible if, for any finite set `A` such that every four-element
subset `B` determines at least five positive differences, there exists a Sidon subset `S`
of size at least `c * A.ncard`. The difference condition is equivalent to
`11 ≤ (B - B).ncard`. -/
def IsAdmissible (c : ℝ) : Prop := ∀ {A : Set ℝ}, A.Finite → (∀ B ⊆ A,
  B.ncard = 4 → 11 ≤ (B - B).ncard) → ∃ S ⊆ A, IsSidon S ∧ c * A.ncard ≤ (S.ncard : ℝ)

/-- What is the supremum of the set of admissible numbers? -/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_757 {A : Set ℝ} :
    answer(sorry) = sSup {c | IsAdmissible c} := by
  sorry

/-- The supremum is strictly larger than `1 / 2`, which is proved in [GyLe95]. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_757.variants.lowerBound {A : Set ℝ} : 1 / (2 : ℝ) < sSup {c | IsAdmissible c} := by
  sorry

/-- In [GyLe95], the authors also prove that the supremum is smaller than `3 / 5`. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_757.variants.upperBound {A : Set ℝ} : sSup {c | IsAdmissible c} < 3 / (5 : ℝ) := by
  sorry

end Erdos757

findings.description:
The docstring says "In [GyLe95], the authors also prove that the supremum is smaller than `3 / 5`", and the Lean states the strict bound `sSup {c | IsAdmissible c} < 3 / (5 : ℝ)`. GyLe95 did not prove a strict bound. They proved (1/2 + 1/(141·76))·n ≤ f(n) ≤ (3/5)·n + 1, which gives only c* ≤ 3/5. Their Fibonacci-type construction has Sidon ratio at or above 3/5; I computed this for the (4,5)-sets {2,3,5,8,...} up to n = 20. The file copied an older revision of erdosproblems.com/757 that read "Gyárfás and Lehel proved 1/2 < c < 3/5". The page has since been corrected to non-strict inequalities.

The Lean claim is still true, but because of a later paper that the file does not cite. Ma–Tang (arXiv:2602.23282) give a 14-point (4,5)-set A_base = {0,136,200,243,246,249,272,286,298,323,400,528,596,1056} whose largest Sidon subset has 8 elements. So every admissible c satisfies 14c ≤ 8, giving sSup ≤ 4/7 < 3/5. I checked this independently by brute force: every 4-subset of A_base has at least 5 distinct differences, and no Sidon subset has 9 or more elements. I also proved `sSup {c | IsAdmissible c} < 3/5` in a scratch Lean file from this set; it uses only standard axioms plus two `native_decide` checks. The mathematics and the `research solved` tag are therefore correct. Only the attribution is wrong, and the evidence for the solved status is missing from the file.
findings.source_evidence: erdosproblems.com/757, current LaTeX (https://www.erdosproblems.com/latex/757): "Gy\'{a}rf\'{a}s and Lehel \cite{GyLe95} proved \[\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{141\cdot 76}\leq c\leq\frac{3}{5}.\] (The example proving the upper bound is the set of the first $n$ Fibonacci numbers.) Ma and Tang \cite{MaTa26} have improved these bounds to \[\frac{9}{17}\leq c\leq \frac{4}{7}.\]" Page history (https://www.erdosproblems.com/history/757): earlier revisions read "proved \[\frac{1}{2}<c<\frac{3}{5}.\]", later corrected to the non-strict version. Ma–Tang, arXiv:2602.23282, §1.2: "Gyárfás and Lehel proved that for all positive integers n, (1/2+1/(141·76))n ≤ f(n) ≤ (3/5)n+1 ... The bounds ... then correspond to 1/2+1/(141·76) ≤ c* ≤ 3/5." Also their Lemma lem:base-block: "The set A_base is a (4,5)-set, and h(A_base)=8", which gives c* ≤ 4/7.
findings.suggested_fix: Option 1: make the variant state GyLe95's actual result, `theorem erdos_757.variants.upperBound : sSup {c | IsAdmissible c} ≤ 3 / (5 : ℝ)`, with the docstring "In [GyLe95] the authors prove that the supremum is at most 3/5." Then add [MaTa26] (J. Ma and Q. Tang, Largest Sidon subsets in weak Sidon sets, arXiv:2602.23282) to the module references, with new solved variants `9 / (17 : ℝ) ≤ sSup {c | IsAdmissible c}` and `sSup {c | IsAdmissible c} ≤ 4 / (7 : ℝ)`. Option 2: keep `< 3 / 5`, but credit it to [MaTa26] (c ≤ 4/7) in the docstring and module references.

reformulations.difference: `IsAdmissible c` requires a Sidon subset of size at least c·|A| in every finite (4,5)-set, of every size including tiny ones (e.g. a 3-term AP has ratio 2/3). The theorem then takes `sSup` of the admissible c. The source's "best constant c" could be read asymptotically, e.g. for n large or with an o(n) error term.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: {c | IsAdmissible c} = (-∞, inf_{n≥1} f(n)/n], where f(n) = min{h(A) : A a (4,5)-set, |A| = n}. In Lean I proved that the set is nonempty (it contains every c ≤ 0), downward closed, and bounded above by 1 (test with A = {0}). So `sSup` is exactly inf_n f(n)/n. Ma–Tang (arXiv:2602.23282, Theorem thm:limit_exists_v1) prove that the optimal constant c* in Erdős's problem satisfies c* = lim f(n)/n = inf_n f(n)/n. Their proof shows f is subadditive by taking the union of A with a generic affine copy qB+t. So the exact reading and every asymptotic reading give the same constant, and the `answer(sorry)` slot asks for exactly the source's c*.

could_not_verify: Gyárfás–Lehel [GyLe95], JCTB 64 (1995) 108–118: I could not read the primary paper, because ScienceDirect serves a captcha. Its bounds come from two secondary sources that agree: the corrected erdosproblems.com text and Ma–Tang's account, f(n) ≥ (1/2 + 1/(141·76))n and f(n) ≤ 3n/5 + 1. On that basis `erdos_757.variants.lowerBound` is faithful, and GyLe95 alone does not give the strict upper bound.
review.notes:
What I checked:
- `IsAdmissible` and `erdos_757` state the source's problem. `B - B` is the pointwise difference set (checked in Lean). For a 4-set, |B−B| = 1 + 2·(number of distinct |b−b'|); I checked this with #eval on {0,1,2,5}→11, {0,1,2,3}→7, {0,1,3,4}→9, {0,1,3,7}→13. So `11 ≤ (B - B).ncard` is exactly "at least five distinct differences". `IsSidon` is the standard B₂ condition. The `sSup` is a genuine supremum: the set is nonempty, downward closed and bounded above, all proved in scratch.
- `research open` on the main theorem matches erdosproblems.com, which marks it OPEN with the page last edited 10 Apr 2026, and the teorth metadata.
- `lowerBound` (1/2 < sSup) is faithful and correctly credited to GyLe95.
- `upperBound` is a true statement. I derived it in /workspace/review/upper.lean from Ma–Tang's 14-point set, with two `native_decide` checks. Only its GyLe95 attribution is stale, hence the single minor finding.

Cosmetic points, not reported as findings:
- All three theorems carry an unused `{A : Set ℝ}` binder. It has no effect, since Set ℝ is inhabited.
- The `IsAdmissible` docstring says "at least five positive differences" where it means distinct differences.
- The file could add Ma–Tang's improved bounds 9/17 ≤ c ≤ 4/7 as solved variants.
- Side remark on the source itself: erdosproblems.com says the upper-bound example is "the first n Fibonacci numbers". The set {1,2,3,5,...} is not a (4,5)-set ({1,2,3,5} has only 4 distinct differences), while {2,3,5,8,...} is. This does not affect the Lean file.

I found no status issues: every category tag matches what the source now records.
